classification.difficultyReason: Identify named angle pairs directly from two marked parallel lines and a transversal.

content.prompt: In the diagram opposite, which angle is:

spec.description: Two rising parallel lines B–C–D and E–F–G, crossed by descending transversal A–C–F–H. Matching single arrowheads mark the parallel lines. All eight point labels are editable. Ordinary source blue strokes are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: B, C, D are collinear; E, F, G are collinear; A, C, F, H are collinear; BD is parallel to EG.
spec.answerVisibility: Point names and parallel marks only; no answer angles or solution annotations.

answer.worked: $\angle AFE$ occupies the same relative position at $F$ as $\angle ACB$ does at $C$, so they are corresponding angles.
The rays $CA$ and $CD$ are opposite to $CF$ and $CB$, respectively. Hence $\angle ACD$ is vertically opposite $\angle BCF$.
$\angle BCF$ and $\angle CFE$ lie between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal, so they are co-interior angles.
$\angle ACD$ occupies the same relative position at $C$ as $\angle CFG$ does at $F$, so they are corresponding angles.
$\angle DCF$ and $\angle CFE$ lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate angles.
